confidence_notes: I ran three of the six allowed web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for local prices. The Arica meal and drink figures come from cost-of-living sites (Nomad Watch, Jobicy, Budget Your Trip, Expatistan). These sources don't agree. Some put a cheap meal at about USD 6 and others at about USD 9. For coffee, beer and pisco sour I also used national and Santiago figures from Preciosmundi (updated July 2026), Expat Arrivals (May 2026), Combien-coute and Nosso Chile (January 2026), then adjusted down slightly for Arica. That gives about 2,800 CLP for a cappuccino, about 3,500 CLP for a domestic beer, about 5,500 to 6,000 CLP for a pisco sour, and about 935 CLP to the USD. Draft beer in a restaurant may cost more than the national average. I could not find a specific price for a glass of wine, so I estimated it from its usual relationship to beer and cocktail prices in Chile. The mid-range meal for two is my own estimate. It is based on the reported USD 14 per person for a good meal and a USD 52 Italian dinner for two that included wine. Accommodation figures are holistic estimates from general knowledge. I did not search for them or check live listings. They are the least certain anchors, because Arica has few registered hostels and July is winter low season, when local and cross-border domestic demand still props up prices.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used national and Santiago prices and scaled them down a little for Arica. Arica is a smaller city in northern Chile, generally cheaper than Santiago and roughly on par with Iquique and Antofagasta for meals and drinks. Its hotel market is mostly modest two- and three-star properties along the coast.
